diagram_math_checks.objects: T is a simplicial tree, g:T→T is the same automorphism without inversions as in the Statement and L1. Only the m=ell(g)>0 case is drawn; x is a vertex off A_g and y its first intersection/projection, as in step 4.1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local Statement, Given, def-edge-inversion-and-action-without-inversions, and proof steps 3.1–4.1. No elliptic or inversion case is suggested by the figure.

diagram_math_checks.maps: g restricts to a bijection A_g→A_g and is drawn as translation to the right, taking y to gy.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 3.1 establishes g-invariance and translation by positive m. Choosing right as the translation direction is a drawing convention, not an added orientation hypothesis. The arrow beneath the axis is expressly an action marker, not a tree edge.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The projection of gx is gy, and d_T(gy,gx)=d_T(y,x)=h.
diagram_math_checks.justification: An automorphism preserves the path metric and takes the g-invariant axis to itself, so the image of the unique branch-to-axis path [x,y] is [gx,gy]. L4 supplies unique reduced paths.

Step 4.1 supplies the decomposition and step 3.1 gives d_T(y,gy)=m. Since m>0, y and gy are distinct; the off-axis branches attach at distinct axis vertices and do not cross or create a cycle. h>0 for a vertex off the axis. Intermediate vertices are explicitly suppressed; page distances do not assert unit edge counts.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The drawn path network has no extra x–gx edge, crossings, or closed cycles; the full axis is indicated by dotted continuation at both ends.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The only solid connections between the four marked vertices are x–y, y–gy and gy–gx, each a possibly subdivided path. No closure is intended. This agrees with the tree and off-axis displacement picture and leaves the rigorous proof independent.
